gaps.sentence: The new model has ___ moving parts, so it breaks down less often.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer moving parts' is correct because 'parts' is countable and plural.

gaps.sentence: She made very ___ mistakes in the essay, so she nearly got full marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Very few mistakes' means almost none, which explains the high mark; 'mistakes' is countable.

gaps.sentence: Only ___ people attended the talk, which was disappointing.
gaps.hint: countable plural; 'only a few' is the natural pattern
gaps.explanation: 'Only a few people' is the standard way to say a small number; 'only few' is not used.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room in here for a piano.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough room' means sufficient space; the negative 'isn't' shows the space is insufficient.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: The hotel was full, so we had to look for ___ hotel.
gaps.explanation: 'Another hotel' means some other, unspecified one; 'the other hotel' would imply exactly two known hotels.

gaps.sentence: I asked ___ in the office, but nobody knew the answer.
gaps.explanation: 'I asked everybody' (all the people) contrasts with 'nobody knew'; 'everything' refers to things, not people.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.
